### [S052.U2] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > G. Compaction of Concrete > 1. Concrete shall be thoroughly compacted, as depositing shall proc...
2. Insert and withdraw vibrators vertically drawing out entrapped air and excess water. Do not use vibrators to transport concrete within forms. Do not insert vibrators into lower layers of concrete that have begun to set. At each insertion limit duration of vibration to time necessary to consolidate concrete and complete embedment of reinforcement and other embedded items without causing segregation of mix. Pay particular attention to providing adequate vibration in the vicinity of sleeves and embeds in heavily reinforced elements and other elements as required. Provide form vibrators to ensure maximum density of concrete.
3. It shall be ensured that the needle vibrators are not applied to reinforcement, which may destroy the bond between concrete and reinforcement. When electric vibrators are in use, a standby petrol vibrator shall always be available at the concreting point.

### [S053.U1] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > H. Construction joints > 1. In large pours, it is practically not possible to carry on concr...
1. In large pours, it is practically not possible to carry on concreting continuously. Hence construction joints shall be provided. Location of construction joint shall be submitted by the Contractor for approval of the ER. Such joints shall be kept to a minimum. The joints shall be at places where shear forces are nil or minimum and these shall be straight and at right angles to the direction of the main reinforcement.

### [S053.U2] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > H. Construction joints > 1. In large pours, it is practically not possible to carry on concr...
2. Form construction joints with a shear key. In walls, do not space construction joints more than 18m apart in horizontal direction, maximum 6m apart in vertical direction

- unless otherwise shown. In framed slabs and beams, and on metal deck slabs, do not space construction joints more than 27m apart. In slabs on grade, do not space construction joints more than maximum 18m in any direction. Place construction joints perpendicular to main reinforcement. Continue reinforcement across construction joints except as otherwise shown.

### [S053.U3] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > H. Construction joints > 1. In large pours, it is practically not possible to carry on concr...
3. Stop ends provided shall have slots for reinforcement bars to pass feely without bending or any other obstruction. Also, a trapezoidal fillet nailed on a stop board shall be provided to form a regular keyed joint. Joints shall be straight and truly vertical or horizontal. Before commencement of concrete placement, adjacent concrete stoppers and surfaces shall be chipped and roughened to expose aggregate, then wire brushed and cleaned. The concrete surface shall be sprayed with water for 24 hours before casting and kept wet until casting. True horizontal joints shall also be provided with a keyed joint by inserting planed greased timber. This shall be treated as above prior to the start of fresh concreting.

### [S053.U4] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > H. Construction joints > 1. In large pours, it is practically not possible to carry on concr...
4. For vertical joints neat cement slurry shall be applied on the surface just before concreting. For horizontal joints, the surface shall be covered with a layer of mortar about 10 to 15 mm thick composed of cement and sand in the same ratio as the cement and sand in the concrete mix. This layer of cement slurry shall be freshly mixed and applied just before concreting.

### [S053.U5] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > H. Construction joints
- I. Expansion Joints
1. Expansion joints shall be formed and located as detailed in the Drawings.
2. Install joint filler to allow the required dimension for sealant, as indicated. Dimensions shown on the Drawings are based on an assumed design temperature of 21 deg. C Concreting procedures shall take into account the ambient temperature range at the time of the respective operations. Do not stretch, twist, puncture, tear, or leave gaps between ends of joint fillers.

### [S053.U6] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > H. Construction joints
- J. Waterstops:
1. Self-Expanding Strip Waterstops: Install in construction joints and at other locations as indicated, according to manufacturer's written instructions and recommendations, bonding or mechanically fastening and firmly pressing into place. Install in longest lengths practicable.
- K. Embedded Items and Inserts:
1. Accurately set anchorage devices by line and transit, and coordinate the locating of anchorage devices to be set for the accommodation of the Work of other trades.
2. Locate anchor bolts as shown on the Drawings and on shop drawings. Obtain necessary templates from the mechanical trades as required for the proper setting of anchor bolts and other items for mechanical equipment, as required.
3. Assist other trades in the installation of piping, pipe sleeves, conduit and similar items where items are to be installed in concrete. Provide frames to securely hold anchor bolts and anchorage devices in place during construction, and take care that no

displacement occurs during the pouring of concrete. Under this Section furnish and set items not furnished by other trades using approved standard type items suitable for their intended purpose.

4. Inserts and embedments shall located as shown in the Drawings and shall be protected from weather and damage in course of the construction.

### [S054.U1] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > L. Openings
1. All required openings and block-outs (pockets) shall be provided as detailed in the Drawings. All openings and pockets shall be de-shuttered with care and all corners of openings shall be preserved. All openings / block-outs (pockets) shall be in a correct line and level. After concreting, the openings shall be secured against any accident by proper coverings, guardrails and warning notices, as appropriate.
2. The Contractor shall clean and grout block-outs / pockets at a later date with a nonshrinking grout mix or concrete of matching strength. They shall be well-cured and protected to correct line and level till handling over

### [S054.U2] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > L. Openings
- M. Filling-In: Fill in block-outs, holes and openings left in concrete structures for passage of Work by other trades, unless otherwise shown or directed, after Work of other trades is in place. Mix, place, and cure concrete as herein specified, to blend with in-place construction. Use non-shrink materials or admixtures as appropriate. Provide other miscellaneous concrete filling shown or required to complete the Work.

### [S055.U1] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > P. Curing
1. After concrete has begun to harden i.e. about 1 to 2 hours after placement, it shall be protected from quick drying with moist or damped Hessian cloth or any other material approved by the ER. Starting 24 hours after placement of the concrete, the surface shall be cured by flooding with water or covering with damp Hessian cloth for a period of 7 days to keep it moist.
2. For the next 7 days the surface shall be kept wet all the time by sprinkling water continuously.
3. For Mass Concrete: Curing period shall be 14 days.
4. For membrane curing, details as listed in 12.5 of SP 24 shall be followed.

### [S058.U2] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.9 FIELD QUALITY CONTROL
Three cubes shall be tested on the 7 th day and other three cubes on the 28 th day.

6. For Mass Concrete, One additional sample shall be taken and reserved for testing at 56 days.

### [S059.U5] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.9 FIELD QUALITY CONTROL > 7. Acceptance of Work
- A. Contractor's Quality Control Responsibilities: Contractor is solely responsible for quality control of the Work and shall develop and maintain a Quality Control Program for the Work.
- B. Certification: Certify, by written report submitted on a weekly basis, for each level, that the elevations, finish lines and building lines of the formwork systems are within specified tolerances, as substantiated by transit survey and that embedments and inserts have been installed within tolerance. Perform survey at locations indicated by the ER (minimum one per bay per floor) of formwork immediately before casting of concrete.

### [S060.U2] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.10 INDEPENDENT TESTING
- C. Monitoring of Concrete Placement: Continuously observe concrete placement operations on a full-time basis, record such observations on a daily basis, and submit reports of the results.
- D. Monitoring of Contractor's Testing: Monitor Contractor's non-destructive strength testing for form removal and termination of curing.

### [S060.U9] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.10 INDEPENDENT TESTING > b. Three cubes shall be tested on the 7 th day and other three cube...
- e. Compression Test Reports: Present at least the following data in tabular form and distribute immediately after recording the test results.
- 1) Identity of job, Contractor, supplier.
- 2) Identity of mix and required strength.
- 3) Pour location of sampled concrete.
- 4) Slump, water content, air content, truck number, time and date sampled, air temperature, concrete temperature, consistency.

### [S060.U10] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.10 INDEPENDENT TESTING > b. Three cubes shall be tested on the 7 th day and other three cube...
- 5) Curing history.
- 6) Date tested.
- 7) Compressive strength.
- 8) Type of fracture.
- 9) Compliance with specifications (yes or no)
- F. Slump Tests: First truck each day, each sample for cylinders, and as often as necessary thereafter. Provide a slump cone and rod available for use at all times. Verify water content in accordance with AASHTO T318, "Measurement of Water Content of Fresh Concrete Using the Microwave Oven" as required by the ER, but not less than one test per day.
